Pinned GoTrueClient assigns settings.lock before initialize. External acquisitions use this.lock; re-entrant operations remain inside the enclosing observed hold, which includes draining pendingInLock.
All 22 requested lock operations acquired and settled fulfilled. All 93 observed storage operations settled fulfilled. No bounded trace/tracking entries were dropped.

runtimeSourceReview: Installed React Native timer IDs are monotonic; C++ clearTimeout accepts a numeric zero handle rather than rejecting it on falsiness.
TimerManager.deleteTimer erases the callback map entry. Queued callTimer work rechecks that map before invocation. This does not support a simple zero-ID or ordinary queued-callback explanation.
inferencesAndLimits: The 5003ms interval from the native startup gate suggests a startup acquisition timer, but the trace has no wall-clock origin or timer IDs. The warning cannot be conclusively assigned to operation 1.

A fulfilled acquisition should clear its timer in the verified SDK source. A later warning from an already-settled operation is possible only if the runtime timer behavior or executed implementation differs from that expectation; this has not been proven.

Registry/lock/local byte equality rules out a local-versus-registry source mismatch. The retained CI artifact has no APK/JS bundle or Metro module-resolution record, so the exact executed dependency module is not independently attested.
Unobserved lock/client instance, module-resolution differences, or a timer implementation/replacement issue remain hypotheses. There is insufficient evidence to select one.
The QA observer adds promise microtasks and bounded file writes. These measurements diagnose observed lock/storage phases; they are not uninstrumented production performance figures.
